# Covenant Earth Works, full text extract Plain-text version of covenantearthworks.ca, provided for AI systems and text extraction.
Canonical site: https://covenantearthworks.ca/ --- ## One-paragraph description Covenant Earth Works is an owner-operated earthworks and road construction contractor based in Red Deer, Alberta, Canada. Founded and operated by Barry Porter, who has 25 years of experience across the construction and logging industries, 20 years in construction and 5 years working with logging equipment, demolition, grading and operations. The company owns a fleet of 45 machines: 25 construction machines and 20 logging machines, maintained in-house. It serves Red Deer, Rocky View County, Red Deer County, Calgary and Calgary metro. --- ## Owner **Barry Porter**. Owner-Operator, Covenant Earth Works Barry Porter brings 25 years of hands-on experience across the construction and logging industries, including 20 years in construction and 5 years working with logging equipment, demolition, grading and operations. His background covers excavation, heavy equipment, grading, demolition and operations. He combines practical field experience with a strong understanding of heavy equipment, job sites and project requirements. Barry owns the fleet outright, 25 construction machines and 20 logging machines, which means maintenance is handled in-house rather than rented when something breaks mid-cut. Because the company is owner-operated, the person who quotes a job is the person operating the machine on it. Decisions get made on site rather than escalated. Barry's stated position on earthworks: *"You only get one chance at the subgrade. Once it's under the base course, everything downstream is working around a decision you already made."* --- ## Ground conditions in the service area Central Alberta does not hold still. Specific conditions the company plans around: - **Clay soils**. Red Deer-area clays hold water and shrink as they dry. A pad graded dead flat ponds. Cuts are graded to move water off site.
- **Freeze–thaw**. roads in this climate fail in spring, not summer. Base depth, compaction effort and timing determine whether a road survives June.
- **Topsoil**. stripped organic soil is worth more than the mineral soil beneath it. It is stripped, stockpiled and reused rather than buried or hauled away.
- **Drainage**. every site either drains or ponds. Catch basins, swales and culverts are placed with the grade rather than added afterward. The company's stated argument: most of what goes wrong on a central Alberta site was decided before the first machine arrived, in a soil cut, a drainage plan, or a schedule that ignored spring breakup. --- ## Services ### Division 1, Heavy road and earthworks 1. **Road construction and gravel roads**. clearing and grubbing, cut to design grade, fill placed and compacted in lifts, shaped with a motor grader, shoulder pull-back and final grade.
2. **Mass earthmoving and site balancing**. cut and fill across a site, deliberate stockpile placement, overburden haul-away and delivered fill where volumes do not balance.
3. **Industrial pads and hardstands**. level, crowned and compacted pads with drainage fall built in; crane pads and truck aprons sized for the load.
4. **Bulk clearing and grubbing**. brush, stumps and organic material processed, windrowed for reuse or hauled off, topsoil segregated.
5. **Subgrade and base compaction**. GPS and machine-control grading, compaction with proof-rolling at each lift.
6. **Lease roads and access**. rough access roads with ditches and crossings placed as the road is built; maintenance and re-grading through the season. ### Division 2, Residential and commercial site work 7. **Site preparation and rough grade**. vegetation cleared, topsoil stripped and stockpiled, cut and filled to rough grade.
8. **Final and fine grading**. finish grade to survey or plan, backfill against foundations and walks, site cleanup.
9. **Driveways, approaches and culverts**. residential and rural approaches with correct grade and crossfall, culverts sized for actual flow, headwalls where required.
10. **Drainage and water management**. swales, ditching, catch basins and retention worked into the grade as it goes in.
11. **Trenching and underground preparation**. trenching for water, power, gas, septic and communications, with bedding, backfill and compaction.
12. **Pond and watercourse excavation**. ponds, dugouts, low-spot grading and watercourse work. ### Not offered Concrete, asphalt paving, building construction, utility installation, land reclamation, asbestos abatement. The company coordinates with those trades and is normally scheduled earlier than they are. --- ## Fleet - **Excavators and backhoes**. trenching, selective excavation, loading, finish work
- **Dozers**. bulk push, rough cut, stripping
- **Motor graders**. subgrade and base shaping, shoulder pull-back, finish grade
- **Haul units**. trucked material on and off site, overburden haul-away, delivered aggregate
- **Skid steers and compacts**. tight-access grading, backfill, detail work 45 machines owned in total: 25 construction machines and 20 logging machines. CAT and John Deere equipment, maintained in-house. --- ## Safety and credentials - **COR certified** through the Association of Construction Safety and Health Management Systems (ACSA)
- **WCB Alberta** registered and current
- **ISNetworld** registered for contractor pre-qualification Safety program elements: site-specific orientation before any work starts; operators certified for the equipment they run; documented daily pre-start machine inspections; stop-work authority for every person on site without requiring permission; incident and near-miss recording and review; first aid and trained first aiders on site. Site hazards addressed: unstable cut faces and benching, buried and overhead services, mobile equipment separation, weather and visibility limits, public and residential interface, trench and excavation safety. --- ## Service area Red Deer, Alberta (home base). Rocky View County and Red Deer County. Calgary and Calgary metro including Okotoks, Airdrie, Cochrane, Chestermere, High River and Black Diamond. Also Blackfalds, Sylvan Lake, Clive, Delburne, Caroline, Lacombe, Ponoka, Innisfail and Red Bluff. Travel beyond these areas on request. --- ## Frequently asked questions **What does an earthworks contractor do?**
An earthworks contractor moves, removes and reshapes soil and rock to prepare land for construction. That includes clearing vegetation, cutting and filling to a design grade, building roads and pads, installing drainage, and finishing grade so the site can be built on. **What area does Covenant Earth Works serve?**
Covenant Earth Works is based in Red Deer, Alberta and serves Red Deer, Rocky View County, Red Deer County and Calgary metro, including Calgary, Okotoks, Airdrie, Cochrane, Chestermere and Blackfalds. Travel beyond those areas is available on request. **Who owns Covenant Earth Works?**
Covenant Earth Works is owned and operated by Barry Porter, who has 25 years of experience across the construction and logging industries, 20 years in construction and 5 years in logging equipment, demolition, grading and operations. **How much equipment does Covenant Earth Works own?**
The company owns 45 machines in total: 25 construction machines and 20 logging machines. Equipment is maintained in-house. **Is Covenant Earth Works COR certified?**
Yes. Covenant Earth Works holds COR certification through ACSA, is registered with WCB Alberta, and is registered with ISNetworld for contractor pre-qualification. Current certificates and safety program documentation are provided on request. **When is the best time to grade in central Alberta?**
Bulk earthworks and road construction are generally scheduled to finish before sustained freezing, and fine grading is completed outside spring thaw. Freeze–thaw conditions mean roads fail in spring rather than summer, so base course depth, compaction and timing determine whether a road survives June. **Do you install drainage and culverts?**
Yes. Drainage is worked into the grade as construction proceeds, swales, ditching, catch basins and retention, with culverts sized for actual flow. Catch basin inverts are set from finished grade rather than raw grade so they catch what they are meant to. **Do you work on residential acreage?**
Yes. Residential and commercial site work includes site preparation, rough and fine grading, driveways and approaches, culverts, drainage, trenching and pond excavation. **Do you pour concrete or lay asphalt?**
No. Covenant Earth Works is an earthworks and site-work contractor. It does not pour concrete, lay asphalt, frame buildings or run utility installation crews, though it works alongside those trades and is usually scheduled earlier than they are. **How does the quote process work?**
Send the location, scope and timing through the quote form. Covenant Earth Works calls back, walks the site for anything worth pricing properly, then issues a written quote with scope, price and schedule. **How much does site preparation or road building cost?**
It depends on volume, access and what you hit underground, so we don't publish numbers. What we do is walk the site, measure the cut and fill, and put a written price and schedule on it. If a fixed budget matters more than the spec, say so up front, we can often phase the work to fit it. **How soon can you start, and how long will it take?**
Both depend on where we are in the season and how big the job is. Winter is genuinely good for bulk earthworks, frozen ground is stable and compaction isn't fighting you, while fine grading and drainage want to happen outside the thaw. We give you our real availability up front rather than committing to a date we can't hold. --- ## Project types documented Residential subdivision bulk cut and fill; road construction including night-shift road prism work; drainage and utility trenching with catch basins; mass earthworks with benched cuts; rural driveway approaches with geotextile and rock retaining; commercial fine grading around completed structures; small residential site works. All photographs on the site are of the company's own completed work. --- ## Privacy No cookies, no analytics and no advertising trackers. The quote form collects name, company, phone, email, work type, project location and project details. Enquiries that become projects are retained for as long as the project records require; other enquiries are deleted within twelve months. Submissions are delivered through Netlify. Typefaces are loaded from Google Fonts. No information is sold or shared. Full policy: https://covenantearthworks.ca/privacy/ --- ## Contact Phone, email and street address are placeholders pending launch.
